findings.issue: The CEO threshold and variance input conflict with A14, the upstream owner of the policy rows. A14 seeds distribution.run.approve as 'amount_cents lte 100000000 and variance_bps lt 2500' = 4E and 'amount_cents gt 100000000 or variance_bps gte 2500' = 6E, and its pass criteria require A$1,000,000.00 -> 4E. A40 says A$1,000,000.00 selects the CEO (amount_gte) and its CEO-boundary challenge and G13 pass criterion expect 6E there. A14's predicate reads a payload field named variance_bps, but A40's payload has only variance_vs_last_bps, variance_vs_forecast_bps and variance_abs_max_bps, so the variance escalation never fires against the real A14. A null variance (zero or missing base) is not handled by A14's exhaustive rows either.
findings.fix: Align with A14: A$1,000,000.00 -> 4E, A$1,000,000.01 -> 6E, 2,500 bps -> 6E. Rewrite the CEO challenge and pass criterion to those boundaries, or reopen A14 if the founder wants the inclusive reading. Add variance_bps = variance_abs_max_bps (absolute) to the approval payload. State what a null variance sends to A14, for example variance_bps = 2500 so the CEO is added when there is no base, or a named resolver added in A14. Test it.

findings.issue: The zero or reduced declaration names checkers that do not exist. A03 row 36 (the canonical maker-checker baseline) is ASTM -> [CFO], [CEO] + board resolution evidence, 6E. A40 says 'ASTM -> CFO + board-role checkers', and its zero-declaration challenge has 'CFO and a board-role checker approve'. None of A03's 51 roles is a board role, so the policy row cannot be built as written. The challenge would test a policy that contradicts A03.
findings.fix: Change distribution.declare_reduced to ASTM -> CFO then CEO (6E), with a required board-resolution evidence attachment (document hash) that A14's precheck checks. Update the challenge to have CFO and CEO approve, and add a probe that is refused without the evidence. Keep who the board is as the existing counsel question.

findings.issue: Sponsor funding can never match. A17 resolves distribution funding through DistributionFundingProvider.expectedFunding(reference) -> { runId, vehicleId, expectedCents, payerNames[] } and says 'A40 registers the real implementation'. A40 never mentions this provider, so A17 holds every sponsor payment as distribution_unknown_reference and no run reaches funded. A17 also holds any amount that differs from expectedCents (distribution_amount_mismatch, resolved only by returning the money), so A40's challenge variant 'funds net + carry_in by mistake: DST_NOT_FUNDED with a 113-cent excess' cannot happen. And nothing stops a second exact payment from matching again and posting step 1 twice, which leaves the run permanently over-funded with no refund path.
findings.fix: Add to the build brief and to sub-agent (2): A40 registers DistributionFundingProvider through A17's index.ts. It resolves reference = run_id (align with A17's 'RUN-...' example or change it to DST-...) to expectedCents = net_cents and payerNames = the vehicle's verified settlement-account names. It returns non-null only while the run is approved or funding and no distribution.fund journal exists for it. Rewrite the over-funding variant: the payment is held by A17 as distribution_amount_mismatch, the run stays funding with DST_NOT_FUNDED naming the full shortfall, and a second exact payment after funding is held, not posted.

findings.issue: The snapshot rule cannot be satisfied with A18's register versions. A18 writes internal versions at 00:00 (or on demand). Only the month-end registry version is certified, monthly, by the trustee (register.certify, REGO -> TP-RE). A40 requires a certified version whose as_of equals the record date, with a default record date of 23:59:59 on the last day of the period. No certified version ever has that as_of: A18's month-end as_of is at midnight, and one at the next midnight falls after the record date. The fallback, an earlier certified version with no acknowledged instruction in the gap, fails for any vehicle with a transfer during the month. A06's September BAY01 run (record date 22 Sep 23:59, with OP-7728, a trustee transfer acknowledged 22 Sep 17:04, and a locked snapshot 'matched') cannot be produced. The spec never says how a certified version at an off-cycle record date comes into existence.
findings.fix: Define the record date as an A18 as_of instant (for example 00:00 on the day after period end, Australia/Sydney). Specify the lock flow: A40 asks A18 for a registry version at the record date and the trustee certifies it (register.certify 4E), or the version is accepted when A18's register_version_compare shows 'match' between the internal and registry versions at that instant. Confirm with A18, reopening it if off-cycle certification is not allowed, and state how A06's 22 Sep BAY01 snapshot was certified. Update the snapshot-gap challenge to match.

findings.issue: The A16 changes this spec depends on are still not in A16's spec, so the build will be escalated at Specify. A16 still has distribution.pay crediting investor_cash + withholding_payable + rounding per line, with LDG_RUN_TOTAL_MISMATCH defined as the sum of pay lines equal to the funded gross. It has no distribution_carry account and no distribution.carry_release, distribution.residual or distribution.pay_bank rows. It has one approval_id column per journal, but step 5 needs both a per-line 4E id and the run's draw. It defines distribution_payable as one account per run, while A40 speaks of a per-vehicle account with a per-run sub-balance. Check 1 asked for A16 to be reopened upstream. Only A40 changed.
findings.fix: Reopen A16 now (plan edit, not at build time). Add the distribution_carry account and the three journal rows with their legs, approval objects and external_ref rules. Move the rounding leg to distribution.residual. Redefine LDG_RUN_TOTAL_MISMATCH as the sum of residual, pay and pay_bank equal to funded_gross_cents. Add a secondary approval reference (line approval) to pay_bank. Use one wording for distribution_payable (one account per run is simplest; then change A40's 'sub-balance' to 'the run's account'). Then drop the 'assumed A16 additions' escalate clause.

findings.issue: The zero-declaration path contradicts the money model. The spec says 'the funding check compares 0 with 0', but funded_gross_cents = net_cents + carry_in, which is non-zero when carries exist. It says the carries 'stay open (carried again)', but calculate reserves them, step 2 consumes them and new pending carries are written. A carry-only line whose carry_in reaches the dust threshold (possible: a no-TFN dust line can carry up to about 188 cents) is paid, not carried, even in a zero run.
findings.fix: State one rule for kind = zero: either carries are excluded (not reserved, funded_gross = 0, no lines) or they are handled normally (reserved, released, paid or re-carried by the dust rule, with funded_gross = carry_in). Fix the zero-declaration challenge to assert that rule's exact carry states and balances.

findings.issue: The carry lifecycle is stated two ways. The carries paragraph says pending -> open when the creating run's step 3 posts. Closure says 'closed ... turns the run's pending carries open'. The nightly distributions.carry_reconcile compares distribution_carry with open plus reserved carries. Under the closure version, any night between step 3 and closure (retrying or manual payout can take days) raises a false Sev1. A later run can also not reserve those carries.
findings.fix: Keep one rule: a carry becomes open in the same transaction that posts step 3. Remove the closure sentence. Add a challenge in which the nightly job runs while the creating run is in retrying.

findings.issue: Step 2 (distribution.carry_release) has no idempotency key and is posted by funding_check before the funding test passes. The job runs repeatedly while the sponsor has not paid. Without an external_ref it can post the release twice. That over-funds distribution_payable, drains distribution_carry and leaves the run stuck with DST_NOT_FUNDED (excess).
findings.fix: Give step 2 external_ref = '<run_id>:carry_release', unique per journal type, so a replay returns the original. Post it once, at the approved -> funding transition or on the first funding_check. Add a challenge that runs funding_check three times before the sponsor pays.

findings.issue: The AML-hold visibility rules contradict each other. Exceptions are 'confirmed by FINA on ADM-19', and the product map's J06 step 3 and ADM-19 mock have FINA reviewing AML holds. Yet the spec and the G14 pass criterion say aml_hold is readable only by MLRO and CCO. Meanwhile lines[] in GET /v1/distributions/runs/{id} and the canonical payment-file CSV (exception_code column), which FINA, CFO and TRSY read and approve, both carry aml_hold. So the pass criterion is either unmeetable or silently failed.
findings.fix: Decide who may see AML holds. Either allow FINA and CFO under need-to-know, as the product map does, and restrict them from investors, sponsors, support and agents of those roles; or keep MLRO and CCO only and mask aml_hold in lines[] and in rendered file views. The hashed file must still bind the true code, so store it but stream it only to MLRO, CCO and the service principal. Make the G14 pass criterion test every read path: lines[], the file download, the A14 payload's exceptions_summary and audit rows.

findings.issue: The guard inputs for A03's SM-08 guards are not mapped. A03 uses one input, approvedTotalCents, in both funding_received (fundedCents = approvedTotalCents) and paid_equals_approved (paidCents = approvedTotalCents). A40's funding compares funded_gross_cents, while closure compares paid_cents with payable_cents, and these differ whenever there is withholding, a remainder or carries. calculated__in_review also requires exceptions_handled (openExceptions = 0), which A40 never feeds. A builder who feeds one value to both guards breaks either funding or closure.
findings.fix: Add a guard-context table: funding__funded gets fundedCents = the run account balance and approvedTotalCents = funded_gross_cents. reconciling__closed gets paidCents = paid_cents and approvedTotalCents = payable_cents from the approved payload. calculated__in_review gets openExceptions = lines with an unconfirmed exception. Test each.

findings.issue: A40's closure checks exceed A20's frozen R8 and R13 contract. A20's R8 is aggregate (the sum of ledger credits equals the approved net, withholding total, bank payouts match the file). A40 requires a per-line match plus the residual journal's remainder and carry legs. A20's R13 recomputes the snapshot file hash, but A40 also has it regenerate the payment file. A40's snapshot_sha256 is 'sha256 of the canonical sorted holder list' with no defined format, while A20 and A18 hash A18's canonical CSV. Closure passes against A40's fake and then fails, or passes vacuously, against the real A20 in A49.
findings.fix: Either do the per-line R8 match and the payment-file re-hash in A40 as a closure precheck (with its own error code), leaving A20 its aggregate R8 and snapshot R13, or reopen A20 to adopt the per-line definition. Define snapshot_sha256 as the hash of A18's canonical CSV for register_version_id (or state the exact fields, order and encoding A20 must reproduce).

findings.issue: The exit run is underspecified. kind = exit has no income period, yet income_period_id is part of the run, draft -> calculating needs A03's income_locked guard, and calculated -> in_review needs sponsor_owner_approved. In the wind-down scenario the sponsor is in default and may have no available SP-OWN. The spec does not say how computeExitWaterfall's residual and per-holder withholding feed calculate(), or how distribution.exit.approve satisfies the in_review__approved guard, which A03 ties to row 35.
findings.fix: Specify the exit path: a synthetic exit IncomePeriod (or a nullable income_period_id with income_locked fed from the locked waterfall inputs), the record date and snapshot rule, net_cents = residual_cents, and whether the sponsor sign-off is replaced by TP-RE or LEGL for exit runs. If that needs an A03 guard variant, raise it as a named A03 extension. Add an exit-run challenge through closed.

findings.issue: Most of A40's approval policy rows have no stated owner. A14 seeds only distribution.run.approve. A06 says A40 registers the row for distribution.run.fund. A40 never lists as a deliverable the rows it must register: distribution.propose, run.fund, line.manual_payout, run.restore_lines, declare_reduced, exit.approve and the AUTO row run.execute with auto_condition file_sha256_equals_approved. Nor does it give their applies_when, which must be exhaustive, their object_ref or their tier labels. The G13 criterion 'thresholds live in policy rows' cannot be checked without them.
findings.fix: Add a policy-row table to the build brief: action code, applies_when, policy code, maker -> checkers, object_ref, auto_condition. Register the rows through A14's registration or seed API from this module. Add a seed test that every action A40 calls resolves exactly one row.

findings.issue: Locking the income period ignores the product map's maker-checker row. ADM-19 lists 'Lock income period' as maker FINA, checker ASTM. A40 says locking 'needs no A14 request' and lets SP-FIN and agents lock. The deviation is not recorded.
findings.fix: Either register distribution.period.lock (4E, FINA -> ASTM) for the staff lock path, keeping the sponsor-side lock as the sponsor's own confirmation, or record the deviation (the lock moves no money; the sponsor owner and CFO approvals cover it) for the founder, with a reason, in Design references or Human gates.

findings.issue: The scheduled payment date has no source. SPN-09 and me/distributions return scheduled_pay_date, and DF-A40-01 and the design need '10 Oct 2026'. distribution_runs has only due_date, which the spec computes as 15 Oct (NSW) or 14 Oct (BAY01 is in VIC). A06 pays on the 10th calendar day. A builder cannot derive 10 Oct from the spec.
findings.fix: Add distribution_runs.scheduled_pay_date, set at create from config distributions.pay_day_of_month (default 10) or entered by the sponsor. It must be on or before due_date, or the run is refused. Use it in both read contracts and in the design-fidelity challenge.

findings.issue: Lateness is detected only for runs still in funding at due_date. A run stuck at the sponsor owner's turn, in in_review, approved, executing or partially_failed past due_date, or a period with no run at all, is never flagged. Investors do not see 'delayed', which breaks the product-map state 'Late: investors see distribution delayed with the reason' and the SM-08 invariant the spec claims.
findings.fix: Make distributions.lateness_sweep flag any vehicle-period whose run is not executed (or that has no run) by due_date. Set late, raise the Sev2 once and require late_reason. Add challenges for a run stuck at calculated and for a missing run.

findings.issue: The APR-2291 design reference contradicts A06's resolution. A06 re-maps APR-2291 to 'Distribution funding · Marion Street · A$20,228.50' (distribution.run.fund, maker agent treasury-drafter on behalf of Priya N., checks carried from APR-2289), with the agent-form audit row. A40 still describes APR-2291 as the Bay Road run approval, defines its check items only as the distribution.run.approve precheck, and quotes the non-agent audit row. The fund request that ADM-30 renders therefore has no check items to show.
findings.fix: Update Design references to A06's mapping. Register a distribution.run.fund precheck that returns the carried items (sponsor owner approved, rent roll attested, snapshot matched, client money covers payout) plus A20 clear. Quote the audit shape 'agent treasury-drafter for Priya N. (Treasury) · Proposed · Distribution funding · Marion Street · APR-2291'.

findings.issue: Cancellation (draft -> cancelled, FINA or SP-FIN) has no endpoint, actions.ts id or G22 row. The agent-parity pass criterion therefore cannot cover it.
findings.fix: Add POST /v1/sponsor/distributions/runs/{id}/cancel and POST /v1/distributions/runs/{id}/cancel with action ids and G22 rows (delegable, amount 0), releasing reserved carries. Add them to the route table and the parity test.

findings.issue: Recovery from reconciling -> partially_failed is undefined when no line is failed or unpaid, for example when an R13 snapshot drift or a non-line break caused the mismatch. Neither retry nor manual-payout-mode is clearly valid, so the run can stall.
findings.fix: State that manual-payout-mode is allowed with zero unpaid lines, moving manual_payout -> executed -> reconciling again once the break is resolved, and add a test for it.
